item.title: Grill-with-docs session — UI design language for Mythoras
item.description: Arcane Cartographer is not locked. The world's cosmological register (technological biology, compiled signal, structural power — not mystical or elemental) suggests a UI language that feels native to that world. Reference framework: RuneScape's data-heavy surrounding frame as primary inspiration for information density, PoE's panel workspace for spatial organisation, Football Manager for the management layer philosophy. The goal: a UI design language that could work across multiple Mythoras-style games, not just this one. Session output: design axioms, not a complete spec.
item.context: Flagged as open design question 2026-06-28. Arcane Cartographer was a starting direction, not a final commitment.
item.gdd-ref: DOC_v6_new §53 — Design System (treat as draft, not final)

item.title: Design session — Regional competition structure and Mythoras identity
item.description: Regional competition needs a distinctly Mythoras identity. References to synthesise (not copy): Pokémon's athlete-journey and gym-badge progression, older Japanese dojo-challenge stories, PoE's varied regional subquests with build-specific rewards (extra passive points, optional strategic paths), Trial of Ancestors faction competition structure (champion-their-tribe escalation, champion status as both achievement and obligation). The Cipher endgame is where Champions participate after winning regional competition — this should feel like a natural continuation, not a mode switch. Open question: keep athlete-journey as the main thrust like Pokémon, or carve something entirely different?
item.context: Flagged 2026-06-28. Competition structure is the backbone of the campaign narrative.
item.review-notes: REOPENED 2026-07-15: competition wrapper plus Examiner/gym-leader naming are not locked. Preserve these references as history only; do not treat the Athletic Circuit/Accreditation/Examiner framing as current canon. See SESSION_DECISIONS_2026-07-15.md.

item.title: Design session — Zone static fixture grammar and map editor spec
item.description: Zones need a static fixture grammar: recognisable landmarks in consistent positional relationships within procedurally generated layouts. Reference: PoE Act 2 Crossroads (waypoint always at the fork, web textures near spider cave, Alira's camp always left from waypoint). The Mythoras Builder's map editor is the right tool to design and test this — build the zone's default structure pre-proceduralization, then the procedural system arranges it. Output: a fixture grammar spec for Region 1's zones, and a map editor feature spec for the Builder.
item.context: Flagged 2026-06-28. Static fixtures enable player pattern recognition and guide-able knowledge without removing discovery.
item.review-notes: Map editor spec ties to BL-009 (Builder zone fixture design)

item.title: Research — RuneScape UI framework analysis for Mythoras data-heavy interface
item.description: RuneScape's UI interface achieves something rare: a data-heavy frame surrounding real-time action without cluttering the play space. It manages information density better than almost any other game in a way that suits data-heavy games (Football Manager, PoE, creature management games). Launch a subagent to analyse RuneScape's UI framework — what structural decisions make it work, what the information hierarchy looks like, how it handles real-time action vs management panels, and what principles could be extracted for Mythoras's own data-heavy UI design. Output feeds into BL-013 (UI design language session).
item.context: Flagged 2026-06-28. This analysis should happen before the UI grill-with-docs session.
item.review-notes: Output feeds into BL-013

item.title: GDD Amendment — Motherboard Grid is global + 5 slot-local subroutes
item.description: The Motherboard Grid was incorrectly described as per-creature in DOC_v2_new and DOC_v3_new. The correct model: ONE global passive tree for the Technician. ONE global route carved by the Technician that benefits all creatures. 5 slot-local subroutes branch off the global route — modifiers apply to the creature in THAT SLOT, not the creature entity permanently. Swapping a creature into a slot changes which slot-local bonuses apply, but not the creature's permanent build. This must be reflected in DOC_v3_new (Progression) §10 and DOC_v2_new wherever Grid is referenced.
item.context: Surfaced in June 28 2026 design session. Also triggers correction to BL-006 — see that item's review-notes.
item.gdd-ref: DOC_v3_new §10 — Motherboard Grid; DOC_v2_new — all Grid references
item.review-notes: Blocks DOC_v3_new update and DOC_v2_new rewrite. BL-006 already annotated with correction note.

item.title: GDD Amendment — Remove Priority tier classification from combat skills

Design philosophy decision: classification tiers invite min-maxing shortcuts and remove interesting decision vectors.

item.title: Stream type effectiveness table (type chart) — Planning Room session
item.description: Dedicated Planning Room session to design the formal Stream type effectiveness table: which Streams deal amplified/reduced damage against which creature Stream profiles. This is the creature-defender type chart referenced in Q6 (grill decision: species-level AND build-earned). The concept is referenced throughout the docs as "type advantage" but the formal multipliers, the number of tiers (neutral / weak / strong), and the full Stream-vs-Stream matrix do not exist anywhere. Must decide: number of effectiveness tiers, specific multipliers, whether Physical is always neutral as the baseline, whether Phenomena Streams have separate rules, how Origin interacts with Stream resistance. Output: a formal type chart table to be integrated into DOC_v2_new §6 or a dedicated §6a.
item.context: GRILL_HANDOFF.md parked items. Q6 locked (species + build-earned). Blocks type-advantage math in DOC_v2_new.
item.gdd-ref: DOC_v2.md §6 Channels and Streams; §9 Combat Archetype System
item.review-notes: Do not invent multipliers in advance. The table must be designed holistically — each Stream's interaction with all 11 others is a deliberate design choice, not a formula output. Structure locked (July 2026 grill): 11×11 Primary vs Primary; soft tiers (0.5/0.75/1.0/1.25/1.5); chart + tag immunities; Secondary as small bias layer ±0.1-0.15×; no base 0× immunities on chart (except authored pairs); Physical as neutral baseline axis.

item.title: Design session — Skill delivery systems (Mines, Traps, Hazards in Turn Program)
item.description: Define trade-off profiles for each delivery tag in Turn Program context: [Mine] (pre-placed, manually detonated, stackable — kills may not trigger creature-local recovery/leech), [Trap] (triggered on enemy entry, single use), [Hazard] (persistent tile damage), [Delayed] (cross-round timing). Key questions: does detonation use Setup or Initiative Window? Do mine/trap kills trigger creature kill-condition effects? How does multi-mine detonation interact with Turn Program commitment model? Reference: PoE Reap+mines as design template (poor self-cast → multiple vectors via mines; mine recovery trade-off). Sandbox identity: proxies circumvent skill weaknesses and create positional depth.
item.context: Raised in grill session July 2026 as off-topic sidebar. Framework tags exist in DOC_v2.md §3.6. Turn Program commitment model (no live intervention) changes some dynamics vs PoE real-time.
item.gdd-ref: DOC_v2.md §3.6 Skill Delivery Tags; §16 Turn Program
item.review-notes: Setup Window vs Initiative Window placement for mine-laying is the key decision. Pre-placement across rounds is the Mythoras-specific value (not cast time mitigation as in PoE).
